correctness.rationale: The rank permutation null is a uniform fixed-composition word. The zero-sum pair-distance identity reduces quadratic bridge energy to weighted pair products. Conditioning on an adjacent color change gives three explicit overlap moments; summing their weights proves the covariance. Fourth exchangeable moments and adjacent/disjoint weighted-edge sums prove the variance. Runs variance follows from adjacent/disjoint transition pairs. Direct rational enumeration checked 55 compositions, 4,072 words, and 330 mean/variance/covariance identities; the proof itself covers all N>=3. The N=2 deterministic boundary and sample-fraction condition for asymptotics are explicit.

value.rationale: The Wald-Wolfowitz and Cramer-von-Mises statistics are standard distribution-free two-sample tests whose dependence affects combined-null calibration. Exact negative covariance across all finite sample sizes, a composition-independent regression slope for integrated squared bridge energy, and a sample-ratio-independent limiting sqrt(N) correlation coefficient provide nontrivial local/global statistic structure. These results are not a renaming or a marginal moment computation.
